subject: general
question: Which type of shank is commonly used on hand reamers?

options.text: Straight shank with a square end
Straight shank with a round end

solution:
The correct answer is __Straight shank with a square end.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Straight shank with a square end__ is the most commonly used shank type for hand reamers.
 
• This type of shank allows better grip and manual operation using a wrench or handle.
 
• Hand reamers are typically used for enlarging or finishing holes to precise sizes.
 
• The square end of the shank is designed to fit a tap wrench or similar tool for controlled rotation.
 
• Hand reamers with straight shanks are versatile and used in various industries for precision work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Morse Taper Shank:**

 
 
• Used in machine reamers to fit directly into the spindle of a machine tool.
 
• Provides self-holding taper for stability during machining operations.
 
 
 
• **Threaded Shank:**
 
 
• Typically used in specialized reamers where the reamer is attached to a machine tool via threads.
 
• Not commonly seen in hand reamers due to lack of manual operation suitability.
 
 
 
• **Straight Shank with Round End:**
 
 
• Commonly found in machine reamers rather than hand reamers.
 
• The round end is designed for collet or chuck holding in machines.
